Especially for that pricetag, it´s definitely worth a shot.
The game is very neatly done.
Though the story seems dull after some time of playing.
First of all: There are many settings that allow you to adjust the game to your taste.
I suppose the developers intented people to play this game in Black and White (while the colour red is the only colour that is always displayed... in colour - yeah sorry about that) BUT they have added the option to increase the colour saturation in this game.
So people who dislike the black and white gameplay, can switch to coloured gameplay as well. +1 for that, even though I like it in B/W.
Further, I recommend to tick the box where it says that you lose all of your loot when you die and that you have to pick it up before your next death, otherwise it will disappear forever.
Might sound harsh and too difficult, but really isn´t. I died three times so far, and each time I was able to pick my loot back up with ease. It just adds to the games atmosphere.
The enemies are... weird. And deadly.
They usually carry bows, knives, pistols or muskets. (so far - I haven´t completed the whole game yet)
If you see an enemy carrying a musket or knife, kill those guys first. It´s quite easy to dodge arrows of enemy archers.
(If the guy with the knife manages to get close enough and stab you, you´re likely going to die. Because they don´t just stab you, but right after they stabbed you and drained about 45% of your HP, they will very quickly draw their pistol and shoot. And that shot will drain the rest of your HP)
The game offers quite nice stealth/sneaking tactics. You can hide in bushes, as far as I understood, you also need to try to not stay in the wind as it carries the sound of your footsteps. So if you have an enemy in front of you and the wind is in your back, he is more likely to hear you.
That is accompanied by a ton of vegetation that indicates the direction of the wind. So that´s pretty cool as well.
Enemies receive increased damage as long as they didn´t see you. So that is quite helpful for players who prefer stealth, as well.
Arrows can ricochet off of the enemies armor (luckily not all enemies have armor) so be sure to either hit the optics in their helmets (basically try to hit their eyes) or other unprotected body parts.
The arrows have close to no dropoff, so most of the times you can just aim directly at their head.
Last but not least, before I say something story-related:
The developers left an email adress in the main menu where you can directly send feedback to them.
That is pretty cool, in my opinion.
+++ SPOILERS BELOW +++
So at this point I want to point out some things in the story, that I have witnessed so far.
One - the story seems very interesting at first, but becomes dull after your first sidequest and talking to the first main NPC.
So there´s that mysterious woman in a red cape right after you leave the beach. And she disappears again after a few seconds. And then she later appears in an abandoned fort and when you talk to her, she says that she wasn´t that first woman in the red cape you saw, but that it was her sister.
Okay.
Further she tells you that she has no idea which enemies you are talking about, because she can´t see anybody besides you on the whole island.
Okay.
So why can´t I bring her with me and actually SHOW her the enemies I am talking about, because all she ever does is, stay in the stupid fort? It could have an actually logical story related reason, but that´s as far as I am right now.
The sidequest I had so far, was basically a ghost that was missing his wife and son. And you are supposed to find out what happened to them.
And here comes a really cool thing.
In Fort Henry, you will find a bell. Upon activating the bell, you can switch into the other world. The black and white colours invert and the whole game suddenly becomes really scary. (Note I´m scared easily)
The game further adds to the scary atmosphere, because you have to "listen" to be able to find quest relevant places in the darkness. And the listening involves hearing ghostly whispers and screams.
-----
There´s more to say about this game, but just go ahead and give it a shot. It´s not the best game, but it definitely isn´t bad. And for that pricetag, you don´t lose much, even if you dislike it.

I've never played a Hitman game before but this is just one awful experience that isn't fun & is overly frustrating.
One of the worst stealth system in any game I've ever played.  There's so many people that you'll be constantly getting seen & when you're in disguise it barely even helps.  If you're disguised as a cook, somehow every cook in the world knows you're not a cook.  Same goes for every disguise.  Like there's some sort of inner circle for every profession in the game.
Once you get caught you might as well reload cause there's a good chance you're not getting out alive.  There's so many NPC's roaming everywhere it's nearly impossible to do anything stealthy at all.  Human shields do nothing to deter persuers.  Cops & whoever else just shoot them until they die then proceed to shoot you.  Firefights in this game are not something you want to get caught up in.  There are too many enemies to handle on your own & you can easily be taken out in a small number of shots.  You can try to run but even that's difficult because of how the game maps are so overpopulated.  Someone will most likely see you if you try to hide & when you do manage to avoid being seen it takes so long to get into your hiding spot they'll probably see you before you get halfway in.
Every mission is poorly designed where there's somehow always someone nearby to see you & because of that it's just one giant frustration.  It's hard to tell where guards are looking & their line of sight is just wierd.  It's supposed to be where they're head is facing but sometimes it just doesn't work that way. One moment you'll be spotted across the map & another you'll be behind someone only to have them turn their head slightly & see you.  There's a minimap radar but there's so many enemies it's nearly impossible to keep track of them all & the radar doesn't track their head movement.  The end result is you being seen more often than you should. It also takes map memorization so you'll get turned around if you don't know exactly where you're going.
The instinct system is especially bad.  It's an energy source that you use to avoid people while in disguise & use a bullet time event that for some reason you have to hold CTRL+Q to activate.  Why can't it be bound to one button? Then when you use it you have to watch a mini cutscene that's supposed to show how cool your kills are but it just makes them take so dang long to finish.  I don't need to see a cutscene every time I kill someone with bullet time. It also drains much too quickly even on normal difficulty & why does it cost instinct to "Hold your hat infront of your face?"
The combat is a mixture of a terrible QTE system for everything that's melee where the text is so small you can't tell which buttons to push.  Even worse is the 3rd person shooting system that is just the most outdated system I've ever had the misfortune of playing.  Even worse is that you're an assassin & you get punished score wise for killing people.  You get punished for getting seen, punished for killing someone shooting at you, punished for nearly every thing you do because you're supposed to be some sort of perfect killing machine even though you just turned on the game.  Then it constantly has pop up messages to tell you when it disconnects from the online scores.  I don't need to be told every single time this happens!
Overall the game isn't bad but it isn't very good either.  It tries too hard to seem realistic & because of that the actual game part suffers.  It ends up with a subpar stealth system, a bad QTE melee combat system, outdated shooting mechanics, an instinct system that makes very little sense, very bad level design, vastly overpopulated areas & it's just a very frustrating experience.

After seeing the future plans of the developer for this game, I feel inclined to write a review.
First of, I got the game in a games bundle, so the 10$ price tag didn´t influence my opinion. If I would have paid 10$ for this game, I would be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ It`s a great example of a Fee-to-Pay game, though not as expensive initially as others.
Let´s start with the overall game: People compare this to Hero Academy and Hearthstone, and the collecting and crafting aspect is really reminisent of Hearthstone. I think the game is better compared with Scrolls when it comes to the battles. It has the same resource system, card based system and turn-based play style as Scrolles. I like Scrolles, and I like this game as a "easier"  Scrolls. So, what´s the deal?
My problems lie in the "Free-to-Play" system of this 10$ game. When I first played it, the pricing was really fair- akin to Hearthstone - you got cards really fast and you could craft your desired cards in a resonable amount of time. But, they made an update to the game since then, that changed the pricing of the card packs and crafting.
So, what changed exactly?
Bear with me on this one, I think it´s important to compare this game to Hearthstone, which is a real Free-to-play (or win) game, meaning no initial price.
If you´re familiar with Hearthstone you know that a cardpack costs 100 gold, this gold is the only currency in Hearthstone, meaning you can also buy it with real money. This game has a premium currency, I´ll talk more about that later, first I want to get to the crafting.
There are 4 rarities in both of these games (Common-Rare-Epic-Legendary).
Hearthstones crafting table goes as follows: Commons cost 40 Dust to craft and give 5 when disenchanted (de), Rares cost 125 and give 25, Epics cost 400 and give 100 and Legendaries cost 1600 and give 400. This means you need 320 commons for a legendary which sounds like a lot, but out of 5 cards in a pack, up to 4 are common.
Before the update this game had a price system that was nearly identical (packs costing 300 in-game money, with 5 cards in each pack, but legendaries and epics were cheaper to make).
Well, after this update, the prices in this game changed drastically. Packs cost 2000 in-game money now (7x rise), whereas the reward for a win rose from 15 to 45... Good luck winning 45 games for one pack.
The crafting prices rose for epics from 400 to make them to 4000 (10x rise) legendaries rose from around 1400 to 8000 (~5x rise), they do give 1000 back when disenchanted. Meanwhile a common gives 4, so you need 2000 commons for one legendary, compare that to Hearthstone again, where it´s 320.
Lastly, the premium currency. It´s extremly overpriced, the upcoming single-player adventure will cost you 30$, a super offer of 42 packs with one guranteed legendary will only cost you around 55$. What a steal!
Before this update the game was great, but now it shows the worst that Fee- and Free-to-Play have to offer.
Stay far away from this if you don´t want to grind for all eternity for every little bit of progress.
P.S.: Please, don´t take this as advertisement for Hearthstone, it was just the perfect comparision, because both ames had a similiar pricing model.

Mini review. Given the nature of the genre, these are my early thoughts.
Picked this up in the recent Bundle Stars Crazy Loot Bundle. Not expecting much I booted it up and was pleasantly surprised in both the depth and scale of the game.
Cards and Castles is a crazy mash up between Hearthstone / Hero Academy and dollop of Chess. I’m fairly new to all these collectible card games and count myself a novice at best, when it comes to the strategy involved in creating decks etc. The tutorial scenario shows you the ropes, as to the basic ruleset and gameplay flow.
Instead of a static board like Hearthstone, the playfield is much like a rectangle chess board with each player's castle positioned at each end. You spent gold to place units on the board and then move them towards your opponent. As in Chess, units have various movement attributes. Extra game mechanics are added with units also having different stats health / attack points. You have spells and static building which add yet more buffs.
I love the artstyle of the game. The 5 different factions all have character and kind of remind me of Kingdom Rush. The music is fairly generic squeezebox medieval type tackle.
Given the size of the Bit Mass team, they should have no hope competing against the behemoth that is Blizzard, in any kind of genre. C&C may not have the polish, but it adds something fresh to mix which is movement / placement of units / buildings. It's a very potent and addictive cocktail of strategy goodness.
I’ve only put in 7+ hours, but I can see myself playing a lot more. To have a hearthstone-esk game on Steam is great and considering what I paid for the game, I’d recommend it to any fan of CCG’s.

I'm a big fat baby when it comes to scary games and movies. I'm not sure how I made it through this one. Maybe the art and play style were fun enough to overcome the scary? I doubt it, because I remember quite a few times I got spooked, jolted in shock, or had my heart racing from anticipation.
Most likely I was able to make it, because the idea of sneaking-out-in-the-open seemed a bit more fun than your normal sneaking-in-rooms type of game. The idea that you should walk while the wind was gusting to mask your foot steps was also a most likely reason. The game does a good job of holding your hand halfway through the first level, but then drops you in a pit surrounded by ravenous beasts. And I do not mean that in a fun way. Perhaps I was not smart enough or maybe I didn't care enough to read every clue, but I couldn't figure out a lot of what I was supposed to do to free all of the souls. Most of them I got, but some of them I had to look online at YouTube videos or guides on where things were. You have to explore each level with a fine tooth comb in both the day time and night time. Then after you find a lost soul, talk to them back to the base, then go back to any previous clues you may of found and you might see a wraith near where they died and where you found a clue to their death. Then after that go back to the lost soul at base, then find another clue. Wash and repeat. I wouldn't of minded the running around chores since the game's atmosphere and environment are fun to run around, but not knowing where to go or not being able to mark anything on your map as a reminder made completing this game impossible for me without the aid of a good guide or two already posted on the steam community and a few YouTube videos.
That being said, if you don't mind having to look up things while you play, I recommend playing this game. It was a lot of fun. I still have to go back for the kill 1000 enemies and stealth-kill 200 enemies achievements.

Cards and castles is a fantastic card game, I've played and won 12 out of 15 games thus far, and I am completely new to the game. The tutorials to the game are extremely useful so If one desires to buy the game or play the game when this eventually becomes free to play, I recommend doing the tutorials, as you will level up decks you have and have time to acquire new cards. Highly recommended the scenarios long before multiplayer is played, for the most part you will be at a disadvantage for the lack of cards gained in the early moments of playing.
This game is rather fair in the fact that all players have equal opportunities to gather the same cards as one another so you will never be at a disadvantage upon completing the tutorial/scenario aspect of the game.
If you're going to play this game and then decide to buy booster packs with the free CP you get, I would strongly recommend playing the draft mode as you are guaranteed a booster pack and a chance to win more for only 450CP. So why wouldn't you do this?
I strongly recommend this game if you like card games, as this is especially close to hearthstone, although as most would probably hate to admit but is a whole lot more fun, for me at least to play this over hearthstone as it adds more of a twist of not only deck creation but unit stances within the actual game itself, heavily introducing more aspects of strategy into the card game.
I've only played 11.9 hours as of current writing review, and I feel a strong amount of hours being placed into the game, and is definitely worth investing into.
The positive
- The game is entirely fair and gives everyone a chance to succeed at the game.
- The game has a strong variety of cards and a vast variety of strategies that can be made.
- The game can be very irratating at times, but isn't this what keeps us coming back for more?
- You can get Easy credit points, currency to buy cards and draft mode with quests every day to give play time a meaning. As well as an easy to understand tutorial that gets you understanding of the games mechanics right off the bat.
- Quick and easy experience to level up fast which offers a chance to level up fast and earn new cards for different factions.
The negative:
- Not so much a negative however, if you're impatient and want to get right into multiplayer, you are indeed going to be at a disadvantage and would be most beneficial for you to get started on the tutorial and scenario for extra cards.
- The game has strong incoming pay to win aspects. The new expansion, which costs a heck ton of money, for minimal bonus cards, and then new cards that require shards to make, make the game stupidly frustrating at times to go against.
Note There is a shop section where you can buy cards and the question would arise: "Is this game pay to win?" absolutely not would be my answer. Although the paying for cards strongly reduces the need to play the tutorial and scenario section for the extra cards and makes acquiring cards much quicker with the use of money. If you wanna save yourself some time and get "starter" decks custom built for you then It's a minimal investment of $4.99 which equates to something like £1.75 to £2.50 which is actually rather decent in comparison to some investments I have seen in some trading card games, Ahem  Magic duels... cough magic 2015.
This game in my opinion has been the most enjoyable 11.9 hours of card games I've played in my life and I am going to enjoy plenty more hours in this game!
I Hope this has helped some of you come to a conclusion on the game, I'll see you on multiplayer!

Probably my all time favorite RTS. Sins is a unique mix of RTS and Empire Builder resulting in a '4X' experience. What this means is you're managing your ships in fights, looking over and establishing research trees, defending, developing, attacking planets and asteroids, doing a handstand, and tapping your heels together all at once. It can be a great blast during those fast-paced thrilling moments. That being said, the game is not at all 'fast-paced' and is slow most of the time. It has a particularly steep learning curve which is not INSANE but you won't know what you're doing by the end of your first game. Still, if you like these types of games and can stick to it - Sins brings a wonderful, unique experience full of phase missiles, laser beams, and cannons. Highly recommend!

Get the pants.
That's what the game is about. The title makes it sound like the game is about leftover food, but it's actually about a pair of underwear the player character's, Tiny, grandfather once owned. You see, this pair of underwear is magical, much like Mormon underwear.
I will say though, this was one of the most interesting platformers I've played in a while, mainly because of the amazing physics and cutting edge laser cutting that was wildly accurate when cutting apart statues, rocks, pillars, etc. The devs did a thorough job of making sure the game has its own art style without trying to imitate platformers of the 90's or the early 2000's. The only difference between this platformer and others is there's no hub world. The game is in constant adventure, through 6 different stages of varying atmosphere, difficulty and length.
The plot is that at the beginning of the game, Tiny gets in a car crash with his radio robot that's trying to guide him, presumably to these pyramids that are seen throughout the game. Well, this other fellow, Big, steals the underwear from the car crash and gains the powers, throwing big rocks and levitaion and what not. Anyway, radio robot helps you along the way while using your tools to fight Big throughout 5 of the 6 stages.
Pretty great game overall though, might have benefited from a full soundtrack of orchestra, platformer music, instead of jams and beats.

Some time ago i wrote a negative review for this game concerning counless bugs that happen on win 10. But the Gods' wish was that I mistakenly pasted it in the box for Titan Quest review without notice. When I found out what I did it was to late, people already started liking the negative review for Titan Quest, and meanwhile I also found the fix for the bugs for The Lord of The Rings: War in the North. So I was forced to write the new review for Titan Quest, and the only fortunate fact is that I here and now can provide information on how to fix buggy LotR: WitN on Win 10:
Open the game folder in Steam folder which should be in you Program Files x86 on the main disc (C). Find the exe file which is  named 'witn' in this path Steamapps/Common/War in the North. Right click on it and 'troubleshoot compatibilty'.
In new window choose first option and click Test Program. The game will run, but it will run distorted with a diagonal line mirrorring the image. This is not enough even though it stops crushing and gliching it look ugly. So quit the game. The window for troubleshooting should have remained displayed. In this window now choose the other option and opt for additional problems. Pick the option that sais that the program runs but doesnt display correctly. Test the game again. From now on game should run perfectly, or at least it is what happened in my case: no bugs, no distortion.
And game itself is lovely, I recommend it openheartedly - 8/10

Wizards should be ashamed of this, even if it IS free to play...
Game starts off by forcing me to participate in incredibly dumbed down introductory tutorials. Why was there no option to skip them? I have been playing MTG for many years, I don't need to sit through the basics. It also felt dumb to me that I had to then click mindlessly through their "skill challenges" in order to get more free gold, since they were basically just more incredibly dumbed down tutorials. What ever happened to the real challenges in these games? You know, the ones that actually made you stop and think about what to do in order to win? These ones are a complete joke.
And the story mode? Complete garbage in my opinion. They give you incredibly basic decks for each of the famous planeswalkers, which you are then supposed to use against the much more powerful AI decks. Seriously?! It's complete BS. This is not even a matter of skill here - the decks you play against are simply way more powerful than yours. I even noticed that a lot of the match ups are against cards with abilities that you have NO answer for in your deck. You basically have to restart until you have a perfect starting hand, then hope that the AI draws as poorly as possible so that you have an equal chance of winning. How is this balanced or fun at all? Also, the fact that you have no idea what cards were added in between missions is incredibly annoying. How am I supposed to know whether or not I even have an answer to something the AI uses against me until I have seen all the cards I have in my deck?
But what REALLY ended the joy for me, was when I was completely robbed of my booster packs that I spent 8 hours forcing myself through the story mode for. No kidding. I decided that maybe I would have more fun if I just simply built my own decks and played against the AI in solo mode for a while, so that I could get enough cards to eventually make a semi-competitive deck for online play. But to my dismay, immediately after spending all my hard-earned gold on booster packs, I was shocked to discover that I was never given ANY of them. That's right, all my booster packs were mysteriously gone right after I spent my gold on them. No new cards in my collection. Nothing. Restarting the game didn't miraculously bring my missing booster packs back either.
The fact that this happened after my initial experience with the game has turned me off from it forever. Do NOT waste your time with this free to play POS. It is literally just a waste of time. You're all better off playing MTGO or the paper version instead.

TL;DR Great for multiplayer......and a White Whale for Single Player
A while back, a buddy and I were on a couch co-op kick, Neon Chrome seemed perfect and it was.  Our first several attempts were cut short as we constantly grenaded each other.  As we became familiar with what the heck was going on and actually communicated, we progressed steadily.  We each fell into niche classes and roles.  Him with the Assassin and stealth, while I charged around wrecking any and everything as the Cyber Psycho.  After the second and third Overseer our process had become...methodical.  We learned the way the AI operated in enough circumstances that we could trap them minimize our damage taken, and...cruel as it sounds....it was fun.  Running those poor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s into un-winnable situations where we waited, weapons at the ready.  We fell out of Neon Chrome after maxing our upgrades and unlocking everything (except for the last Cyberware...which I STILL don't have....dammit)  and we moved on to other projects.  However, Overseer 4.0 sat there in his chair....mocking me.  I had made it to floor 23 on a solo run...I could get him...I could kill him.  I obsessed over getting enough credits to fund a maxxed out run from the bottom to the top.  If I was going to overthrow that maniacal a**....I was going to do it right.   And I did.  But then there was overseer 5, and 6....Now I am 56 hours deep and I have met with my greatest foe.
Overseer 8.  He has consistently shut me down with waves upon waves of troops, and a Caretaker that seems nigh indestructable.  This game truly is just a series of processes to me now.  I have reached the point in this game where others stop seeming fun, and yet I play on.  I know the numbers just get higher, nothing really changes anymore...but I need to know.....just how many Overseers are there?  When does it end?!  When have I won?!!?!
Resounding Recommendation

Just a few quick impressions, and quirks a potential purchaser should be aware of:
1. Early Access or not, no game should ship without a Pause or Save Game feature. Too many interruptions in the modern world. The awkwardness means I'll play less than I'd planned. If these features exist, they are not mentioned. Anyone?
2. Can't choose your month to fish. I choose September, I get July at night. I choose May, I get.. July at night. Really? Another turn off. This is a must fix. Why have good graphics(See, something nice), if you can't see them? New fish are nice, but the basics are, or should be, the priority.
3. The rod positioning could use some polishing, at least eventually. No line or rod in real life could stand up to the sharp angles, especially when  the fish gets within 20m feet or so.
4. I hope that eventually, some fish sign will be added, like swirls and tail splashes, and a variety of fish shapes and shadows as the fish is brought into play. A bit bare right now. Save and pause and date choice are priorities.
5. A few nice things. I've watched The Great Rod Race 2, and this game has the potential to bring that style of fishing to life for me. Hope the devs can make a go of it. I chose this game over the competition as it seemed better supported.
My first fish was a 20 lb carp. Lost a 30-40+ lber when the net wouldn't sit right. Got to move the fisherman forward to hit the right spot to place the net. Casting is next to impossible on higher resolutuions, the bar moves faster than the response. LIttle tricks to learn, and that's ok. Bream and tench and various carp are kinda fun.
*** This is too good. Caught a 40lb plus carp, made the top 50. Ok, but when I went to photograph it(flash camera, anyone?), it was not there. Couldn't break back to the fishing either, until I hit "Y" to reset camp. Instead, that command led me back to fishing, where the description of my big fish and the overall list remained. A fish hit another bait, and, upon setting the hook, I noted that the line and rod tip were no longer connected and only the rod could move, not the now disconnected line. A magic rod! I landed the fish, believe it or not, by noting where the movement of the screen made it logical to find the fish with the net. You can't make this stuff up, its too good.
Overall, what will make or break this game for me will be how convenient it is to play. I want to fish when I want to fish, not when the game says I can. Saves and pause features are  a must for continued play, and soonest. I was a beta tester for VR Sportfishing, an almost great game which fell by the wayside despite many advantages over other fishing games. Hope this one does better.
More later, unless a better fishing game comes along. Fisherman can be as picky and fickle as the fish they strive to catch. Remember that, devs. Can't recommend it yet. Lots of potential here, like a new found pond that might hold a good fish. Good luck!

Carp Fishing Simulator mentions it's the most advanced authentic fishing sim on the market. They were not wrong. After playing recent games like Dovetail Fishing which seemed very arcade focused, I was pleasantly surprised at just how much of a simulation this game is. Time of day, weather and peg selection all play a huge role. Don't expect to catch a fish every time you cast, patience is
and if you want to hook the big ones some knowledge of bait, line and rig setups is huge plus.
With that said you don't need to be a professional either. Amateurs can  randomly select bait, have a little patience and enjoy a relaxing day catching fish. I'm the first to admit many of the options went well over my own head as we catch mostly bream, barra and coastal fish in australia. Was still able to land a few 25 odd kilo carp, sizable catfish and plenty of smaller stuff which brought a smile to the dial. Far more then just carp fishing as well. At the moment the game contains several species of carp, catfish, bream, perch and tench with plans to add more species in future. Fish AI was a real highlight, all placed into the lake with no pre-scripted movements or behaviors. Releasing fish could use some tweaking but the catching part itself feels quite good.
Graphically speaking it's reasonable for a sim. Setting up your tent and lines around the nearest snag point on the lake while watching the sun slowly drop behind the hills can really help on those stressful days. Would like to see more detail added to the surrounds but it's passable. Fish all seem to be the one size, reeling animations and a few other things need work but nothing missing that's gamebreaking. One nice feature is the leaderboard which shows all the catches around the world and how you match up, in recent patches it now stores all these for future bragging rights to friends.
Other plans that I'm aware of is adding online multiplayer, different ways of fishing, new locations and character creation, along with tweaking and refining the whole experience of course. Carp Fishing Simulator can only get better from here and it's a game I can highly recommend keeping your eye on to any fishing or simulator enthusiast. Cheers folks and happy gaming/fishing. :)

Carp Fishing Simulator review
I know I only have a few hours in CFS, but this game doesn't have much to offer at the moment.

CFS has some pretty graphics that don't need you to turn it on the highest settings to enjoy. Although it does require quite a tough computer to run CSF on maxinum graphics which is quite dissapointing. The water looks better than in most games, the trees look quite realistic, the Carps are absolutely amazing but the only things that needs improving are the fishing rods and baits. There are a few camera effects in the game which adds some points to the final score and also give me a sign of hope for the future of Simulation games. There's a ton of baits that look fantastic for a game this early in development since almost everyone of them is different to eachother.
In CFS you can fish. However it is not as easy as you might think. You'll need to custiomize your fishing loadout with new baits, different hooks, different lengths and so much more. Then you will need to find a spot to try your luck for a fish in, wait some time, then check what Carp you (hopefully) found! It is very exciting once you found your first few fish, but once you found a strategy that works for you, it feels as if you've just cheated. The customization is absolutely amazing, you can change nearly everything in your setup including where your camping spot is. There's not much fish that you can try and catch (this is
fishing simulator) since there's only a few species in this game. Sadly enough, this simulator doesn't have all that much game to it apart from fishing and customizing, so I'm afraid CFS will need to lose some marks for that. However, it is fun to play in short bursts to just play around in the loadout section. You also can't try and escape from the game by drowing yourself or using a car.
There's currently only one, small and quite depressing map that consists of pools of water, some trees, some bases, a dock (plus a boat), a car park and a very creepy building with photos of Carps being held by random people. This isn't the best quality for a pricey game. So if you like some impressive maps, this isn't the best choice for you.

Stylish dark/noir arcade shoot'em up. Very nice graphics, animation and effects. Simple but addictive run and gun, and dodge and aim. Each level seems fairly open with a degree of exploration and side missions.
Gameplay consists of exploring varied environments such as a town, sewers, wilderness, moving train cars, in a 3D isometric style 3rd person perspective, using radar to find and eliminate the vast majority of denizens of any given place. You can carry 3 guns + 3 types of grenades, have limited ammo, can also sprint, dodge roll, and kick people within proximity to stun them or kill them.
The level of detail and fluidity in the graphics and animation is what we should have expected from something like Wasteland 2. I would love to see a mod turning Hatred into an action RPG shooter, or somat.
I'd say the game could take a $5 drop in price, considering it does become a bit repetitive, although its fun to play a level or two at a time without becoming too fatigued.

There's not much to say about Hatred, mainly because there is not much to do in Hatred. This game was wonderfully advertised for its controversy which is what has made the game so popular in the first place, but if only their ability to build hype was as good as their ability to build a decent game. If maybe a bit of extra thought or purpose was given to the game it might hold it's own a little, but shortly after the opening few minutes you have already done everything that you can.
Graphically, the game has quite a nice gritty visual style which holds up in my opinion; the ability to smash through the destructible environments is a nice a touch. The violence, in terms of blood and gore, is actually fairly tame in comparison to many games that I have played which recieved nowhere near as much controversy. I guess context is probably what puts it into the AO ranks, though personally I don't think it deserves a rating that high; getting it an AO rating only surged its media publicity as being one of the few games to earn that rank.
All in all, this game shocked me, not because of it's pointless violence, frustrating controls (especially with a keyboard) and lack of any narrative at all, but just because it was boring and lacking in any substance at all. I'm all for video games being an open and free platform for people to create whatever they want in anyway they want to, but I am not for this game being used as an example for that statement as there is much more out there from Indie studios who deserve the publicity for a game that inspires further creativity and something positive.

I bought Civ5 being an avid fan of the series which did not give me the urge to try Civ:BE. But it was on free trial for a weekend and so obviously I thought I should try it.
It's a better game than Civ5 in my mind. It adds a lot more thingybobs and ideas and the tiny improvements you get feel as if they make a difference. The battle is reduced a lot in complexity. There are very few unit types in this game, but instead of researching new unit types, you upgrade your units as you research techs that increase your ideology, which is a nice idea. If your idea of playing civ is to be the first to create a 4:1:1 unit and smash up your opponents out of the gate, you won't find any support for that tactics in this game.
I would also add that they made the relationships a bit more straightforward (you attacked me, I dislike you)
I only wish there was some way to automate the trade routes rather than having to relaunch them all every few moves.
So if you enjoyed Civ5, I would recommend that you try BE as well. It improves on all the little problems in Civ5.
But what about the big problems from Civ5? That it takes 10 minutes to start a new game? That if you play it on big maps it slows to a crawl and is barely playable? That despite taking so much time, the AI is still completely stupid? Nope. No consolation there. It's still a good game but also still a horrible piece of software. You will still spend 5 seconds on making a few moves and then 2 minutes on watching a progress bar. Oh, yeah, and automated exploration units still need you to watch over them.
I very much appreciated the free trial, it confirmed my conviction to not buy the game.
So if like me you thought Civ5 was an abomination, stay away from this game. Firaxis has some good game designers. Now they need some decent software developers.

tl;dr Buy it on sale
HERE'S WHY:
I don't want to call it a problem, BUT-
The over-arching problem with this game is its length. It's too short. Now I wasn't dissatisfied with the game, I wanted there to be more; more blocks to slice, more sliced blocks to pull, more pulled sliced blocks to rocket thrust, more wide open areas with simple yet engaging scenery, but as I said before content quantity is this game's shortcoming.
But fortunately this brings me to positive points.
What this game is is a large scale 3D platformer in which the goal is to go from point A to point B through the manipulation of large chunks of stone to work your way through very large areas (primarily ancient ruins) full of platforms, bridges, pits, tunnels, secrets rooms, the whole lot. Utilizing your three tools effectively provides a wide palette of techniques to progress through each level: whether you create a bridge to reach another platform, or create a ramp down to a platform with potentially more resources, or maybe you're like me and you decide to strap a rocket to the back of a stone slab and surf your way to your goal. But the point is nothing is set in stone (everything is stone hah get it) here, you make your way to the magic pants in whichever way pleases the tastes of your inner mason.
The story, while short, is both simple and goofy as well. Take that as you wish, but unless you have a fetish for black briefs and have a lifelong feud with your brother, the story is a meaningless accessory to what is actually fun gameplay.
So in summary yes, I like the game and I'd pay 99 cents for the game again, full price however, no.

I beat the game on hard.  It took 7 hours.  It wasn't easy.  I don't think it was a shallow shooting game by any means.  The system of executing people for health is conceptually silly but it leads to some tense gameplay later in the game when almost everyone has a gun.
Levels are large and have interesting layouts and options for cover.  I've seen some reviews say that cover in this game doesn't work and this is just a twin stick shooter, but in the later parts of the game you won't do too well without crouching behind everything you can.  When it gets harder it almost becomes an overhead cover shooter if you are playing it right.
The destruction is the coolest looking feature and probably one of the coolest gameplay elements.  Being able to make the cops/army trap you in a corner, just to blow an escape hole with a grenade, and then flank your pursuers through a window makes this a more interesting affair than just popping out from behind corners all day long.  Grenades are plentiful for about half the game, too, so there is a lot of opportity to make rubble.
One thing I think is odd that people aren't really mentioning is that this is basically an exact remake of the original POSTAL.  Not all of the levels are the same, but they both feature a similar perspective, a main character in a duster, a mission to murder everyone and nothing more, similar weapons, half dead enemies crawling on the ground and struggling to breathe and gurgling blood, and they both start out at the main characters house.
Only complaints are the camera makes it so that it's always easier to go north, but some levels make you come back south, forcing you to use different tactics just because your view isn't as good.   The game is a little short at 7 hours, but not bad for the price.  It was a crazy fun 7 hours, though.  And the black and white is kind of blah, I wish there was a cheat for color.
If you enjoyed the original POSTAL, or Crusader: No R---- games, then you'll understand the minor control issues here and probably love this game.  Or if you just like really awesome looking destructive violence.

I REALLY wanted to like this game. I reinstalled it 4 separate times to give it a chance...but I just don't enjoy the repetitive, undocumented, and quite frankly boring gameplay.
As another reviewer said:
"Admittedly, until the repetition really comes to light, the game does thrill with its sheer originality. The problem, really, then, is that the repetition comes far too quickly."
PROS:
-Good art style
-The different character set playthroughs are legitimately different
NEUTRALS:
-Sound is good at first, but gets to be very repetitive quickly
CONS:
-EXTREMELY repetitive.
-NOT randomized in many aspects. Levels are static. Snow is exactly the same duration, people show up at exactly the same days, etc.
-Success in this game is based more on what you know (ie guides or brute-force memorized from previous plays since a lot is not randomized) rather than on how well you actually play the game. The lack of documentation on many things is a serious issue and leads to massive amounts of guessing on what things do (if anything).

-Very little UI information (esp with regards to the character's status and how it changes as well as the chars special "ability")
-Melee Combat is RNG and consists mostly of just clicking on the enemy and hoping to win the dice roll. And yet, the knife backstab with certain characters is an instant kill that is game-breaking good (Again, this is not actually explained anywhere so as a new player you will have absolutely no idea why sometimes you hit the enemy and sometimes they  hit you...well, its just pure RNG based)
-Extremely slow gameplay (especially during the day)
*Daytime gameplay usually consists of eat and build an item or two and then you just end the day (around 8am...) unless you need to trade....but since there is no fast forward, you just get to sit around staring at the wall until midday when the trader guy shows up. Some "events" do happen during the day (which generally is a guy knocking on the door to ask for help, give you supplies, or trade with you) but since there is basically nothing to do during the daytime, you either end the day early in the morning or just sit around (literally) staring at the walls until midday for the event to trigger....but since you don't know what days the events trigger this means you have to wait EVERY day (just to find out nothing happened) or you end up skipping days where events would have happened....
I really *REALLY* wanted to like this game. I played it "naturally" (no guides and a different story each time so the items were different) and did NOT reload cheese at night.

This War of Mine is one of the most emotional, grim games I've ever played. There were many moments in this game where I felt absolutley terrible for the things I had to do to survive. WARNING: this is not a happy game in any stretch of the imagination. This is a game about war, and war is hell. Sure there are a couple mildly happy moments in the game, but overhall it's very grim. This War of Mine is a game based on the Seige of Sarajevo that lasted 1,425 days and it is known to be the largest seige of a city in history. You play as a group of civilians trying to survive in a fictional beseiged city called Pogoren. You must deal with starvation, lack of medical supplies, scavangers trying to raid your supplies, and the emotional state of the survivors.
One of the best things about this game is the fact that I couldn't reload a previous save to undo a horrible thing I've done, the game only auto saves after every night of scavenging and override's the previous save. This makes it more emmotionally gripping and nail-biting since it makes my decisions perminant and that it made me try even harder to not die. And it's not easy, trust me. There are multiple points in the game where I had little resources and my survivors were either starving, depressed, exausted, freezing, or all of the above. All of the abbandoned buildings were either stripped clean of supplies or didn't have the resources that the survivors needed to, well, survive.  There were only 2 options: raid another shelter for supplies or die. I had to rob and/or kill (mostly) innocents for their supplies in order to survive. It's not a walk in the park either, it will be emotionally heavy for both the player (unless they're a psychopath or a sociopath) and their survivors. The one who got to raid and kill the innocents for food and supplies will suffer from severe psychological trauma. And the player will have to deal with that.
And due to the trend I've seen when people who review this game tell a story from their experience from the game, I'm going to do that too.
There was one day where my survivors were starving, some wounded and/or exausted. They had little resources, their options were limited. They had no choice but to attack another Shelter full of people. Marko, an expert scavenger, couldn't go because he was emmotionally broken from all the people he had to kill in order to survive. Bruno seemed to be the only one capable to go and steal from another shelter, so he was sent to steal supplies from another shelter while Pavle was to gaurd the shelter from looters during the night. When Bruno reached the place, he looked through the peephole and saw a gaurd. He waited when the gaurd wasn't looking. Bruno then equiped his knife and then stabbed the gaurd in the back. This didn't insta-kill him though, so Bruno had to stab him a second time. Bruno then looted the gaurd's corpse and found a shotgun with some ammo. This caused some noise however, and caused a woman to come down from the stairs. The woman was crying out: "Oh god! Herald, no! No, this can't be happening!" and sat down next to the dead gaurd while sobbing. Bruno couldn't think striaght, he thought it was best to shoot the woman and put her out of her misery. The gunshot alerted two gaurds nearby, they came down and saw the two dead bodies of their comarads. They yelled out "Murderer!" to Bruno and tried to kill him. Bruno killed the two soldiers but was severely wounded. As he looted their corpses as well as the nearby area with no gaurds, he was soaking in the fact that he just murdered innocent people for food.
I felt like crap after doing that, there are many moments like these that the player will encounter during their playthrough. It's depressing but in a good way, if that makes any sense.
But the game isn't perfect, the survivors will sometimes say obvious things like "this shovel is doing well." while they're  digging it. And the controls can be annoying at times, I've accidentally closed doors when I was trying to get through them multiple times in the game.  It runs pretty smoothly on my pc, and I haven't noticed any bugs sp far.
But the game's flaws hardly take away from the experience. This is by far my game of the year. I give This War of Mine a 10/10. I highly recomend it if you're sick of war games from the point of view from a soldiers perspective and glorifying violence.

TL;DR - Tepid recommendation for co-op if on sale
+ Twin stick mechanics are spot-on
+ Fun weapons, some of which will be familiar to Crimsonland players
+ No bugs in co-op play that I came across
+ Largely destructible environment is a great mechanic, especially during boss battles
+ Great retro soundtrack
+/- Loot system tries to straddle a grab-n-go weapon system (like Crimsonland) but with some RPG-lite elements.  In my opinion it doesn't do either well, and should have stuck to one or the other.
+/- Boss battles are tolerable, with the different phases not really differing much in strategy or challenge.
+/- Story has potential, but is largely meh
- Limited camera view; camera doesn't elevate to accommodate co-op players when they spread out, and your movement is limited to the camera view.  This results in lots of entrapment on screen that require your buddies to come back for you.
- In co-op,  you're getting shot at from off-screen the majority of the time (see camera issue above)
- Environment and art style, while cool, gets repetitive
- Little variation in level design, except that later in the run, many more rooms to become purposeless with enemies but no loot, keys, etc.
-- In co-op, you don't get any more health help in the levels than in solo.  I feel like this is a major oversight.  For solo it's dialed in just right in my opinion, but for co-op, the difficulty of keeping your health up far exceeds the difficulty of any other aspect of the game.  This, along with the camera issues mentioned above that ensure you're getting shot at by off-screen enemies, make it a very frustrating co-op experience.
This game was fun in co-op for a few hours, eventually becoming too frustrating due to the above issues and without any real great reward system to keep us going.  I'd say it has about $5-worth of co-op fun in it.

After playing the game for a while I can tell you it needs serious work.
The trading is unenjoyable, the game doesn't help explain anything more complex than keybinds. Some might try to defend it saying it is a steep learning curve but that implies that the game attempts to help you learn. Tooltips on everything would be extremely helpful. If I would suggest anything it is a tooltip system like Crusader Kings 2 where it gives you the conditions to be met or a good description of what is being done.
The player faction AI is absolutely terrible. My ships don't even defend themselves, they don't attack targets which I tell them to, I have low ability captains but the option to "Train" them is never explained or available.
The UI is okay in some aspects and horrible in others. It would be nice to have filters for stations selling and buying certain products on the map. The map has the most problems as it is really unhelpful when you are trying to find certain buildings in space. That being said I've had a lot of problems buying things only to realize I bought it for the wrong ship, which coincidentally cannot actually sell anything because it has a lack of cargolifters. Maybe a prompt straight up asking which ship you want to use that isn't ignorable would be much more helpful.
Player ship combat is decent. There are a lot of different munitions to choose from for missiles but my main energy powered weapons seem very limited.
The minigames are simply stupid. Many times I've landed in areas that aren't "purple" and "scored" but sometimes I get it in the purple and the game still fails me. If this is the route you want your game to go then at least make it more defined. Honestly I hated the minigames the most.
Controlling other ships is mostly a hassle. Creating a station seems very important but it is woefully underexplained in the campaign "tutorial". Although the one thing I do like is docking in capital ships. That is awesome and I love how I can see the outside while it is flying me across the galaxy.
The voice acting for NPC's is god awful. Different lines are few and far between. It seems like whenever I talk to female traders they keep asking me if I want to see their boobs and my captain has expressed their joy in meeting me for the first time... for the tenth time.
Graphically this game is pretty decent. Not AAA material but good. Although the NPC models are extremely bland. It's like everyone is bald except for my energetic rebellious do-gooder copilot.
I have no way of really gauging how good my ship is compared to others except by looking at their armaments. What good is telling me how much flat damage my missiles do if everything is only measured in percentages?
Hireling skills really confuse me. What exactly is the difference between a 1 star and a 5 star? In a game governed by trading and numbers it seems this was an afterthought. Honestly a lot of the percentages and numbers in this game feel very meaningless. Like my cargo allows me to have so much m3 but I can only carry so much of one item. It should probably give more information about this in ship details.
The plot of the game is decent, but it really railroaded me along and it felt like that was the only thing that gave the game any meaning. Also, I changed back my ships name from Albion Skunk to Albion Pride but they keep calling me the Albion Skunk, probably should lock the ability to change the Skunk's name.
All in all the game feels very empty. I liked the premise but I don't like the feel of this game.
This game is very casual compared to the other titles in the Hitman series, but if you want a comfy game where you sneak around and kill people, this could be a good game pickup.

First Impressions:  This game has been out for a while but I just got it this month in the Humble Bundle.  Wow.  What can I say other than that it is a hell of a lot of fun and challenging at the same time.  I am only at the 4th floor and I fell in love with this game back on the 1st floor.  It is the perfect date that keeps getting better.
Easy to learn; hard to master.  The graphics are top-notch for a top-down shooter.  The gameplay lacks nothing (other than me blowing my face off with a rocket because I did not see the spiderbot in front of me).
The sounds are exactly what they should be.
The music...oh the music.  The soundtrack in Neon Chrome is nothing short of phenomenal.  Jonathan Geer spins a slick web of 80s music mixed with "right now" music.  There are so many spots in this soundtrack that I stop what I am doing and just live in the moment of the music.  The music could not have been more perfect, and especially for this game.  10/10 music.

If you enjoy Shadowrun, you should get this game. The music is that haunting, ballad-esque outrun style that almost tells a short story on it's own with no lyrics. The atmosphere is grim and entertaining without becoming too repetitive. The combat is awesome for a twin-stick style shooter.
It's a "roguelike" as we've come to know them; get as far as you can while collecting money to buy upgrades to get as far as you can next time. Though this one handles the story aspect of a loop in a sort of clever way, and you can basically swap between your "NG" and "NG+[...]" status before each run if you want.
There's a large variety of weapons each with their own qualities that you may like or not, and from what I can tell they are all balanced very well. The only aspect that doesn't quite make sense to me is the DPS calculation you see when you compare weapons, which you do by standing over one  you could pick up. Say weapon A has a higher rate of fire, a higher base damage, and a higher crtit chance, but a lower "level," sometimes the DPS will show as less than weapon B for some reason. Maybe I'm missing something.
The combat is incredibly satisfying. Burst fire weapons, shotguns, etc, they have an impact. I don't know if it's just visual or if it's the visual combined with the immense ramping of damage that comes with hitting multiple shots for X damage and crit modifiers and seeing enemies just drop, but it feels really good. the maneuvering is great, the AI sort of works like a time-warped stealth mechanic in other games. If humans lose you, they drop pursuit and sort of pathfind around less intently which allows you to lure them if you need to, and their pathfinding in general allows you to slip them. IE: dart around a corner and double back through a hallway to end up behind them before they get to the corner, and sometimes this is absolutely necessary.
When you do things like this it just feels really good, from picking up the loot to meleeing a rocket out of the air at the last second, this is basically a twin-stick shooter in the Shadowrun universe, unofficially, but even without the "outrun" style it would be a damn good twin-stick on it's own.

You almost don't have to do hardly any side missions in order to progress to the end. I feel like SR4 required completing a lot more of your side quests before the end.
The problem is when the main story progresses they give you no choice if you'd like to wait and continue other missions. You're flying along on a side mission, Dane calls and will say "hey I need you now", or "X weapon is ready", etc., etc. and the game stops in the middle of what you're doing and teleports you to that scene. Rushed cutscenes pushing you further along. Next thing you know it's go see Satan. Unfortunatly they don't make it very clear that once you do that's the end. The weak boss battle against Satan doesn't really give you a clue either. Yeah you're fighting Satan but it's so easy it feels like a pre-battle to the final. But it's not. So, if you really like SR and just have to add this to your collection I'd say wait until it's under $5.

It had been a long time coming for the 2001 release of Return to Castle Wolfenstein. The last main title in the franchise to be released was Wolfenstein 3D: Spear of Destiny in 1992, which saw the subsequent release of two mission packs, Return to Danger and Ultimate Challenge, in 1994. Needless to say, fans of the series were sure that it was dead, left to be a relic of the past, albeit an important one that birthed first-person shooters. However, when the genre expanded into the realm of more advanced 3D graphics, id Software seized the moment to resurrect Wolfenstein from the brink of extinction.
Putting its first spin on a richly detailed story arc, the introductory cutscene of Return to Castle Wolfenstein dates back to 943 AD where Heinrich, a German prince who dominated Western Europe with his army of the undead, is stopped by a monk who seals him in an underground tomb. Fast-forward to a thousand years later in 1943, Heinrich Himmler, the Chief of the Nazi SS, is researching any possible way to win World War II through a combination of science and black magic. In doing so, Himmler comes across stories of Heinrich, and becomes deeply interested in bringing the German prince back to life, and as such the SS Paranormal Division is born. Our fated hero, B.J. Blazkowicz, and his partner known only as Agent One, had been captured by Nazi forces and taken to Castle Wolfenstein to be tortured for information. Blazkowicz survives, his partner does not, and he must escape the Nazi compound and stop Himmler, Deathshead, and their abominations.
If you've played any shooter from the early 2000's, then you'll already know what to mostly expect from this title. However, the action is incredibly fast-paced, a trait that has stayed a series staple even through the most recent installments. That being said, there are missions that require stealth, as setting off an alarm will result in a game over, which is a series first for Wolfenstein. In fact, being stealthy in missions that do not require such acts is beneficial to the player, since the damage that is taken by any bullet whatsoever is ridiculously high, which in turn makes the gameplay difficult even on the easiest setting.
There is a ton of diversity over the course of 7 chapters, which are separated into 26 missions. From snowy tundras, to open compounds, narrow villages with multiple buildings to explore, creepy catacombs, vast castles, and even a graveyard. The atmosphere is thick, with many levels being laden with cobwebs, mist, fog, and even lightning; not to mention, explosions galore. There are also a good amount of enemies to face off against, ranging from the standard Nazi SS and paratroopers to skeletons, mummies, and deadly mutant abominations. Likewise, there's no shortage of weaponry to use to take down these foes; flamethrowers, Panzerfausts, Stens, MP 40s, Colts, Lugars, and more await use, including the electricity-using Tesla and a Nazi-invented machine gun known as Venom.
Return to Castle Wolfenstein is the first chance that the series had to really dig its heels in and tell a worth-while story, which it does really well through various cutscenes and written briefings that appear before each mission. There are also many odes and nods to Wolfenstein 3D and its predecessor, Spear of Destiny, and even Blazkowicz's escape from Castle Wolfenstein is a mirroring of the first and second episodes of Wolfenstein 3D. The atmosphere of the game is worth lumping into a horror-inspired category, as many of the levels deal with resurrected skeletons, mummies, supernatural entities, and sci-fi mutants. Even if you are someone who didn't enjoy playing the two retro FPS titles in the franchise, Return to Castle Wolfenstein may very well distill your taste for the series, as it's one of the very best early-modern FPS games to date.

This game, in many ways, mirrors some of the accomplishments of F.E.A.R. (for obvious reasons); for instance, it forces players to choose and use a small selection of weapons at any one time, and the game has a sense of immediacy in its control scheme lending itself to direct action (I half expected to nail enemies with flying kicks). The otherwordly effect of a child's voice conjured experiences of Alma Wade, as does the duality found within the persona and actions of the antagonists' structures. With these similarities in mind, is Betrayer a good game?
Yes.
Betrayer is a good game, and stands on its own merits: a strong narrative, striking presentation, and effective use of audio. The dependence on audio cues is rewarding. Dialogue between the player character and non-player characters are accomplished through simple trees, whose options are unlocked when clues are discovered. Roaming the world of Betrayer harkened to Silent Hill, but was animated and alive in a way that allow a player to imagine themselves in the midst of a breathing, sighing forest, tinged and tainted with subtle blood-red cues. When action happens, the player's speakers tend to explode with a rushing, beating heart, and enemies are deadly.
The challenging enemies serve to emphasize the theme of the game, and its narrative. There is a lot of text in Betrayer, and it is well-written; the investigations often reveal cruelty or tragedy, and all tie into the eponymous conceit of the game. I'm not sure if spoken dialogue would have improved things, because voice acting on a budget can do more harm than good, and often precludes narratives from achieving the depth text otherwise provides.
While well written and compelling, the text of the game can sometimes be confusing. Players have to backtrack and search areas again, which made the later game feel systematic rather than fluid.
Stick with it and its rewards will yield themselves.

I wasn't sure what to make of Betrayer when I first saw an advertisement for it a few months ago...a first-person action/adventure game set in the 1600's and rendered in a heavily contrasted, black and white environment similar in style to the wood etchings of the time period? Sounded interesting in the very least. The trailer was convincing too but it was still in Early Access on Steam and I wasn't in a pay-to-test mood so I put it on my Steam wishlist and promptly forgot about it.
The Steam Summer Sale, 2014 re-acquainted me with this title and I was thrilled to pick it up for a mere $5.00 via the digital distributor. I dove into it immediately and became obsessed...
'I awoke, washed up on shore as the waves lapped the stone-strewn beach around me. I immediately realized I must have sustained a head injury during the storm that tossed my ship against the rocks for I was color-blind! Dizzy, my head aching, I pulled myself from the sandy, salty froth that ebbed and flowed around me. I lurched to my feet and stumbled over to a nearby crate, still wobbly from my ordeal and headsore, shielding my eyes from spray of brine and piercing rays of sunlight alike.
Armed with a sturdy tomahawk and an old longbow I stumbled through the surreal landscape my damaged eyes showed me, making my way towards Fort Henry, the coastal stronghold for the colonies I was sent to investigate for the Crown...'
Indie developer Blackpowder Games has crafted an exquisite experience for anyone willing to brave the chiaroscuro the game initially presents to the player. The familiar control scheme and minimalistic interface become immersive strengths as the artistic design seemlessly meshes with the twitchy, responsiveness of the Unreal Engine, drawing you in with austere beauty and heart-pounding action alike. To top it off the story is very well done and relayed to the player through various elements ranging from visual clues to conversations with ghosts.
After a while I got sick of the black and white motif and was pleasantly surprised to find the in-game visual options which allowed me to colorize the graphics and adjust contrast elements. Game developers often cut costs on graphics by skimping on texture quality and dressing their graphics in post-processing effects that cover up glaring flaws. This is NOT the case with Blackpowder Games and the colorized textures are very detailed, even up close.
The sound design is also very well done and positional audio is relied upon often for clues and direction in the large, woodland areas that lend themselves to becoming lost in. Furthermore, I encountered no game-breaking bugs and the most annoying glitch I encountered was the graphical artifacting and tearing I found, which was mostly mollified via tweaking video settings.
However immersive and compelling the game elements are, Betrayal has some negative aspects depending upon individual preferences. Weapons and the enemies you fight with them are very limited and there is not a huge variety of anything in the game world. The player is locked into the FPS perspective and there is no ability to zoom out with the camera, which can be tough on people who get motion sickness from such experiences. The combat is very twitchy and dodging enemy fire is important to survival thus hand-eye coordination is paramount to success in Betrayal. The in-game map is unmarkable and there is no mini-map overlay so keeping track of places of interest and your relative position in an area can be tedious.
In summary, Betrayer is an excellent first effort from Blackpowder Games. It's a great example of what talented game developers can do with a limited budget and a time-tested game engine. Minimalism has been played to great strength in this title, resulting in an immersive experience populated by tragic tales, beautiful environments, thrilling combat, and expertly designed mechanics. A satisfying romp for any fan of FPS action/adventure games.

All that is served in a very basic form and doesn't really contribute to a deeper immersion, but it certainly adds a little thrill to a mindless hack'n'slash button mashing activities.
That all said it's a decent title that can be obtained cheaply these days and played in a spare time.

I always thought this game was pretty alright, mostly cuz when I was younger, I remember getting this game as a Christmas present right around the same time I finished actually reading LoTR, and nothing was cooler than seeing that cover.
The story isn't gonna blow you away, and it certainly isn't Tolkien tier world building, but the characters are all very reminscent of the way J.R.R. wrote characters, which is kinda dry and boring, but very endearing and very likeable. The writers do a pretty good job of making this seem like a legitamate thing that could have been happening alongside the original story, giving detail into a part of the world that Tolkien had mostly left alone, I felt. The game also does a good job of tying everything that's in it to the world of Middle Earth. Nothing just randomly happens or seems out of the blue. And really novel stuff happens, like instead of having a big stupid battle with a dragon, you talk to it and strike a deal with it. Seeing a lot of old, memorable and loveable Tolkien characters is always a nice touch as well.
It's worth noting, too, that this game is not technaclly cannon, which is actually kind of a shame. Some of it is, like I said, pretty good and interesting, but I get why it can't be cannon.
The gameplay itself is pretty... bland. Its repetitive, has no depth what-so-ever... but its easy to do and beat the game, so its not off putting or anything. I'd gripe about it more, but the game has lots of writing going on to keep you interested, so the gameplay is an ignorable flaw.
I read around through some other reviews and saw that lots of people were having problems with bugs, but I didn't notice much of anything when I played through the game. That being said, I only did so once, and have also played through the game on the 360 and PS3, so perhaps I overlooked some things.
Overall, I think $20 is a pretty good price for this one. It is, I might add, MUCH more enjoyable playing with some friends. So, if you have any, definatly consider War in the North.
